summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of systemic lupus erythematosus, chronic abdominal pain, and recurrent hematemesis presented with three episodes of vomiting blood and severe epigastric pain radiating to the back. She had undergone an EGD eight days prior with no acute bleeding source identified. In the emergency department, nasogastric lavage was negative and stool was heme-negative, suggesting no active gastrointestinal hemorrhage. She was admitted for observation, started on IV fluids and medications including a proton pump inhibitor and anti-nausea treatment, and advanced to clear liquids. Despite medical recommendations to remain hospitalized, she requested discharge against medical advice due to dissatisfaction with pain control and concerns about missing specialist notes. She was discharged home with instructions to advance her diet cautiously, continue her home medications including prednisone and methotrexate, and seek immediate care if symptoms worsened.
